witnesses.question: Do simple candidate-authored data-contract assertions retain Unicode, missing versus null, malformed-record ordinal/raw text and source-sensitive invalidation?
witnesses.expected_behavior: Exit 0; accepted=2, rejected=1 at ordinal 3, raw rejected record retained, Unicode α and null/missing distinct, stable in-memory source digest, changed source key differs.
witnesses.code:
import hashlib, json
from datetime import datetime

raw_lines = [
    '{"id":"α","ts":"2026-01-02T03:04:05Z","note":null}',
    '{"id":"β","ts":"2026-01-03T03:04:05Z"}',
    '{"id":"γ","ts":"not-a-time","note":"bad"}'
]
source_bytes = ("\n".join(raw_lines) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
source_hash = hashlib.sha256(source_bytes).hexdigest()
accepted, rejects = [], []
for ordinal, raw in enumerate(raw_lines, 1):
    obj = json.loads(raw)
    try:
        stamp = datetime.fromisoformat(obj["ts"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
        accepted.append((ordinal, obj["id"], stamp.isoformat(), "missing" if "note" not in obj else ("null" if obj["note"] is None else "value")))
    except (KeyError, ValueError) as exc:
        rejects.append((ordinal, raw, type(exc).__name__))
assert accepted[0][1] == "α" and accepted[0][3] == "null"
assert accepted[1][1] == "β" and accepted[1][3] == "missing"
assert len(accepted) == 2 and len(rejects) == 1 and rejects[0][0] == 3 and "not-a-time" in rejects[0][1]
assert hashlib.sha256(source_bytes).hexdigest() == source_hash
assert hashlib.sha256((source_hash + "|contract-v1").encode()).digest() != hashlib.sha256(("changed|contract-v1").encode()).digest()
print("accepted=2 rejected=1 ordinal=3 retained=true unicode=α null-vs-missing=distinct source-bytes-stable=true source-key-change=invalidates")
